nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group. The number of irreducible complex characters of $G$, that is, of functions $G \to \mathbb{C}$ that are the character of some simple finite-dimensional complex representation of $G$, equals the number of conjugacy classes of $G$.
nodes.title: Number of irreducible characters

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group and $k$ a field. For every finite-dimensional representation $V$ of $G$ over $k$, the character of $V$, the function sending $g \in G$ to the trace of the linear map by which $g$ acts on $V$, is a class function on $G$.
nodes.title: Characters are class functions

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group and $k$ a field. For every class function $f : G \to k$ and every $x \in G$, the function on conjugacy classes that corresponds to $f$ under the linear isomorphism between class functions and functions on conjugacy classes takes the value $f(x)$ at the conjugacy class of $x$.
nodes.title: Evaluating a class function on conjugacy classes

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group and $k$ a field. For every function $q$ from the set of conjugacy classes of $G$ to $k$ and every $x \in G$, the class function that corresponds to $q$ under the inverse of the linear isomorphism between class functions and functions on conjugacy classes takes at $x$ the value of $q$ at the conjugacy class of $x$.
nodes.title: Lifting a function on conjugacy classes

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group and $k$ a field, and write $[x]$ for the conjugacy class of $x \in G$. This is the $k$-linear isomorphism from the space of class functions $G \to k$ to the vector space of all functions from the set of conjugacy classes of $G$ to $k$ that sends a class function $f$ to the function $[x] \mapsto f(x)$; its inverse sends a function $q$ on conjugacy classes to the class function $x \mapsto q([x])$.
nodes.title: Class functions as functions on conjugacy classes

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group and $k$ a field. The space of class functions $G \to k$ is the $k$-linear subspace of the vector space of all functions $G \to k$, under pointwise addition and scalar multiplication, consisting of the class functions.
nodes.title: The space of class functions

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group and let $f : G \to k$ be a class function with values in a set $k$. If $x, y \in G$ are conjugate, then $f(x) = f(y)$.
nodes.title: Class functions agree on conjugate elements

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group and let $f : G \to \mathbb{C}$ satisfy $f(hgh^{-1}) = f(g)$ for all $g, h \in G$. Suppose that for every simple finite-dimensional complex representation $W$ of $G$, with character $\chi_W$,
nodes.title: A class function orthogonal to all irreducible characters vanishes

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group and $k$ a field. The space of class functions $G \to k$ is a $k$-vector space whose dimension equals the number of conjugacy classes of $G$.
nodes.title: Dimension of the space of class functions

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group and $k$ a set, and write $[x]$ for the conjugacy class of $x \in G$. A function $f : G \to k$ is a class function if and only if there is a function $q$ from the set of conjugacy classes of $G$ to $k$ such that $f(x) = q([x])$ for all $x \in G$.
nodes.title: Class functions factor through conjugacy classes

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group and $k$ a set. A function $f : G \to k$ is a class function when it is constant on conjugacy classes, that is, $f(h g h^{-1}) = f(g)$ for all $g, h \in G$.
nodes.title: Class functions on a group

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group and let $(V_i)_{i \in I}$ be a family of simple finite-dimensional complex representations of $G$ such that $V_i \cong V_j$ implies $i = j$. Then the characters of the $V_i$ are linearly independent over $\mathbb{C}$.
nodes.title: Characters of nonisomorphic simple representations are linearly independent

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group. The irreducible complex characters of $G$, that is, the functions $G \to \mathbb{C}$ that are the character of some simple finite-dimensional complex representation of $G$, are linearly independent over $\mathbb{C}$ in the space of functions $G \to \mathbb{C}$.
nodes.title: Irreducible characters are linearly independent

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group and let $f : G \to \mathbb{C}$ satisfy $f(hgh^{-1}) = f(g)$ for all $g, h \in G$. Then $f$ is a $\mathbb{C}$-linear combination of irreducible complex characters of $G$, that is, of functions $G \to \mathbb{C}$ that are the character of some simple finite-dimensional complex representation of $G$.
nodes.title: Irreducible characters span the class functions

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a field, $G$ a group and $\rho$ an irreducible representation of $G$ on a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space $V$. Then $\rho$, viewed as an object of the category of finite-dimensional representations of $G$ over $k$, is a simple object.
nodes.title: Irreducible representations are simple objects

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
